junction.name: 1st Avenue South & Southwest Michigan Street, Seattle

claims.text: 1st Avenue South & Southwest Michigan Street had 34 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.3 million a year.
56% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck motor vehicle, rear end” crashes, against 30% at the city's worst crash locations.
42% of crashes here happened on a wet or icy road, against 19% at the city's worst crash locations.
41% of crashes here were recorded as “rear ended” crashes, against 13% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 9024, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $32,000 a year.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 1.6 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $554,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 1st Avenue South, Highland Park Way Southwest, Southwest Michigan Street, unnamed (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
